RAJYA  SABHA
————
List of Questions for ORAL ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Thursday,  the February 26, 2009/Phalguna 7, 1930 (Saka)
————
(Ministries: Prime Minister; Atomic Energy; Coal; Communications and Information
Technology; Development of North Eastern Region; Environment and Forests;
External Affairs; Finance; Housing and Urban Poverty Alleviation;  Information
and Broadcasting; Overseas Indian Affairs;  Panchayati Raj; Parliamentary
Affairs; Personnel,  Public Grievances and Pensions; Planning;  Shipping,
Road Transport and Highways; Space; Statistics and Programme
Implementation; Urban Development;
Y outh Affairs and Sports)
Total number of questions — 20
49
Development of infrastructure and
connectivity
*141. SHRI B.J. PANDA:
MS. MABEL REBELLO:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government is aware that
development of infrastructure and
connectivity is the single most important
factor to remove regional disparities;
(b) whether Government has
formulated certain specific anti-poverty
programmes with focus on infrastructure
and connectivity especially with reference
to Orissa and Jharkhand States; and
(c) if so, the details thereof?
Incident of roof-fall in coal mines
†*142. MISS ANUSUIYA UIKEY:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that an incident
of roof-fall in Moari mine of Chhindwara
district in Kanhan area had taken place in
recent days;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor;
(c) the details of the losses due to this
roof-fall and the cost thereof;
(d) whether there is no warning system
or assessment of possibility of such
incidents and whether it could not be
prevented; and
(e) the official responsible for this
incident who was supposed to make efforts
to prevent this incident by prior assessment
of the same and the action taken against him?
Depletion of foreign exchange reserves
*143. PROF. ALKA BALRAM
KSHATRIYA:
SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA:
Will the Minister of FINANCE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether a large amount of the
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

50
country's foreign exchange reserves has
depleted in the last six months;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor;
(c) whether the fast depletion of foreign
exchange reserves has serious implications
and depreciation on the value of rupee; and
(d) if so, the steps Government
proposes to take in this regard?
Permission for erection of surface
structures in coal-bearing areas
*144. SHRI R.C. SINGH: Will the
PRIME MINISTER be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
is giving permission for surface structures
such as airports, buildings, complexes, etc.
in the coal bearing areas of the country;
(b) whether it is also a fact that
unauthorized people have also occupied
some of the coal belts in the country which
otherwise deprive the country from
extracting India's primary source of energy,
i.e. coal; and
(c) if so, the reasons behind giving
permission for such structures and what
rehabilitation steps Government is taking
or proposes to take to rehabilitate those
people who are under occupation of such
land which contains coal reserves?
Extradition treaty with Nepal
*145. SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA: W ill the Minister of
EXTERNAL AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) whether India and Nepal have
decided to modify the existing extradition
treaty that would allow the two countries
to hand over criminals of third country;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether the nexus between trans-
border criminals is increasing and in the
absence of an extradition treaty, criminals
are freely enjoying; and
(d) if so, the reaction of Government
thereto?
Relocation of human settlements in
Wayanad Wildlife Sanctuary
*146. SHRI K. CHANDRAN PILLAI:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to
state:
(a) whether he has received a project
proposal from Kerala Government for
voluntary relocation of human settlements
in Wayanad Wildlife Sanctuary;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) the number of tribal and non-tribal
families to be relocated;
(d) the total cost of the project; and
(e) the status of the clearance of the
project along with the details of the amount
sanctioned and released, so far?
Protection of migrant labourers
*147. SHRI RAMACHANDRA
KHUNTIA: Will the Minister of
OVERSEAS INDIAN AFFAIRS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that thousands of
migrant labourers in middle east countries
are not getting their wages and legal dues
and many of them are still inside jail on
false fabricated cases; and
(b) if so, the action taken by
Government of India till today to protect
the migrant labourers in middle east
countries?

51
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
Exemption in recovery of loan to
farmers
†*148. SHRI SHIVANAND TIWARI:
DR. MURLI MANOHAR
JOSHI:
Will the Minister of FINANCE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Rs. 32,000
crore is due as loan with farmers who hold
five acres and more of agricultural land in
the country;
(b) if not, the facts in this regard;
(c) whether any scheme is under
consideration of Government for certain
exemption to be given in recovery of the
loan; and
(d) if so, the outline of the scheme and
the number of farmers in the country who
would benefit from this scheme?
Debt relief to farmers
*149. SHR I RAMDAS AGARWAL:
SHRI OM PRAKASH
MATHUR:
Will the Minister of FINANCE be
pleased to state:
(a) out of the budgetary allocation of
Rs. 60,000 crore given as debt relief to the
farmers during the financial year 2008-09,
how many farmers have taken advantage
of loan waiver scheme indicating the total
amount of loan reimbursed/outstanding
against them, State-wise, till date;
(b) whether loan taken by farmers from
the private lenders has also been waived
off; and
(c) if so, the details thereof?
Pakistan State actors' role in Mumbai
attacks
*150. DR. T. SUBBARAMI
REDDY:
SHRI GIREESH KUMAR
SANGHI:
Will the Minister of EXTERNAL
AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) whether USA is convinced that
Pakistan State actors played a role in
Mumbai attacks and US has endorsed
evidence gathered by India through FBI
about complicity of Pakistan State actors;
(b) if so, whether this has brought
changes in Indo-US relations;
(c) whether US terror package for India
has been approved;
(d) whether Pakistan terrorist king was
held in Nepal by Nepal Government;
(e) whether Iran has also stated that
Pakistan must use iron hand on terror; and
(f) if so, action taken by Pakistan in
this regard so far?
Fall in tiger population
*151. DR. GY AN PRAKASH
PILANIA: Will the PRIME MINISTER
be pleased to state:
(a) whether latest census shows sharp
fall in tiger population;
(b) if so, the details thereof and
Government's reaction thereto;
(c) tiger population in States/tiger
reserves in 2002, 2007 and at present;
(d) whether the situation is alarming;
(e) the total amount spent by Centre/
States till date, since inception of tiger
project, viz. World Wildlife Fund for tiger

52
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
conservation in India, average annual
expenditure for upkeep and protection of a
tiger;
(f) the details of observations of
Rajasthan High Court on 25 May, 2007
regarding corruption/mismanagement in
Ranthambhor National Park, and whether
similar lapses are rampant in other tiger
reserves also; and
(g) the steps being taken to salvage the
situation?
Defective ATMs
†*152. SHRI JAI PARKASH
AGGARW AL: W ill the Minister of
FINANCE be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government is aware of the
fact that due to defective Automated Teller
Machines (ATMs) of many public sector
banks, consumers are often unable to
withdraw their deposited money from
A TMs and they are facing many difficulties;
(b) whether there is any shortage of
technical employees to repair A TMs; and
(c) the measures taken by Government
to ensure smooth functioning of A TMs and
to protect the interests of depositors?
Depiction of violence, obscenity and
vulgarity on TV
*153. SHRI MATI VIPLOVE
THAKUR: Will the PRIME MINISTER
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government is aware of the
fact that depiction of violence, obscenity
and vulgarity on the television (TV) is
increasing;
(b) if so, the reaction of Government
thereto;
(c) whether Government has taken any
steps to check depiction of violence,
obscenity and vulgarity on the television;
and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
Use of Chinese handsets
*154. SHRI PRAKASH JAV ADEKAR:
Will the Minister of COMMUNI-
CATIONS AND INFORMATION
TECHNOLOGY be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that cheap
Chinese handsets are selling in Indian
markets, which do not have an international
mobile equipment identity and these pose
a threat to India's security; and
(b) if so, the details of measures
Government is taking or contemplating to
take to ban cheap Chinese mobile handsets
as most of the countries have strictly banned
this kind of electronic devices?
Doubling of India's loan entitlement
*155. DR. JANARDHAN
WAGHMARE:
SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA:
Will the Minister of FINANCE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether in view of recession and
decline in foreign investment, Government
has approached World Bank to double
India's loan entitlement;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) the present position of borrowing
of loans by Government from foreign
agencies;
(d) the interest to be paid by
Government on such borrowings; and
(e) the steps taken by Government to
make payments of the principal loan
amounts?

53
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
Ganga Action Plan
*156. SHRI AMAR SINGH:  Will the
PRIME MINISTER  be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government is aware that
more than 1.4 billion litres of untreated
affluent is flowing into Ganga river daily
and at a number of places the quality of
water is worse than when the Ganga Action
Plan was initiated on which Rs. 1500 crore
has been spent, which has gone down the
drain;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor;
(c) whether Government has chalked
out any time bound plan for cleaning Ganga
river; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
Propagation of schemes by PIB
*157. SHRI PRAVEEN RASHTRA-
PAL: Will the PRIME MINISTER be
pleased to state:
(a) the details regarding Public
Information Campaign by Press
Information Bureau (PIB) and other media
units in the States of Gujarat, Maharashtra
and Madhya  Pradesh having sizeable tribal
population; and
(b) the steps taken by Government to
provide sufficient officers, staff and other
logistics to the PIB media units in the above
States to propagate various schemes
through audio-visual medium?
Number portability
†*158. SHRIMATI SUSHMA
SWARAJ: Will th e Minister of
COMMUNICATIONS AND INFOR-
MATION TECHNOLOGY be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that there is
unnecessary delay in implementation of
number portability;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor; and
(c) whether any time-frame has been
fixed for implementation of number
portability; if so, the details thereof?
Indians languishing in foreign jails
†*159. SHRI A VTAR SINGH
KARIMPURI: Will the Minister of
OVERSEAS INDIAN AFFAIRS be
pleased to state:
(a) the number of Indians languishing in
jails abroad, along with the details of the
charges against them;
(b) the details with regard to their
names, addresses etc., State-wise and
district-wise; and
(c) the steps taken by Government to
get them released from jails and the details
thereof?
Sales tax on petro products
*160. SHRI MOHD. ALI KHAN: Will
the Minister of FINANCE be pleased to
state:
(a) whether there is any proposal to cut
sales tax on petro products to reduce their
prices further;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) if not, the reasons therefor?
N
EW DELHI; V . K. AGNIHOTRI,
The 20th February, 2009 Secretary-General.
Phalguna 1, 1930 (Saka)
